# MercuryResource

> Domain research archive for Mercury. Literature reviews and primary-source analyses. Curated by Corgan Studio, Inc.

Research Archive: https://mercuryresource.net/research/ (literature reviews by Corgan Studio, Inc., open to read).

## Research Archive

- [BepiColombo flyby magnetic-field signatures and Mercury magnetosphere context](https://mercuryresource.net/research/bepicolombo-flyby-magnetic): Review of the BepiColombo Mercury flyby magnetic-field measurements through 2024, the cross-comparison with MESSENGER's orbital baseline, and the implications for Mercury's offset-dipole structure and the cusp-and-current-sheet topology.
- [Caloris Basin and the antipodal weird terrain: impact dynamics and seismic propagation](https://mercuryresource.net/research/caloris-basin-antipodal-terrain): Review of the Caloris Basin impact structure and its antipodal weird-terrain expression, with focus on Mariner 10 and MESSENGER mapping of the basin floor, the implied impactor dimensions, and the seismic-focusing model for the antipodal disturbed surface.
- [Mercury libration and the liquid outer core](https://mercuryresource.net/research/mercury-libration-liquid-core): Review of the radar-and-spacecraft measurements of Mercury's forced libration in longitude, the implied decoupling of the mantle from the inner core, and the consequent constraint on a liquid outer core layer that supports the dynamo.
- [Mercury's polar volatile deposits: MESSENGER neutron spectrometer evidence](https://mercuryresource.net/research/mercury-polar-volatiles): Review of polar-volatile evidence at Mercury, from radar bright spots through MESSENGER neutron-spectrometer hydrogen mapping to MLA reflectance, with implications for ice origin and BepiColombo follow-up.
- [Mercury's tenuous exosphere and sodium tail dynamics](https://mercuryresource.net/research/mercury-sodium-tail): Review of Mercury's surface-bounded sodium exosphere and the comet-like sodium tail observed at Earth-based and orbital observatories, with focus on the source-and-loss processes, the latitudinal asymmetry, and the seasonal modulation tied to Mercury's orbital eccentricity.
